newsitem.title: USA: August wholesale inventories surged as sales dropped.
newsitem.headline: August wholesale inventories surged as sales dropped.

text.p: Inventories of unsold goods on wholesalers' shelves climbed to record levels in August as sales dropped at the sharpest rate since the start of the year, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.
Overall inventories rose 0.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted $260.31 billion -- the highest level on record and the biggest monthly increase since a 1.2 percent surge four months earlier in April.
Inventories fell a revised 0.1 percent in July instead of rising 0.1 percent as the department reported a month ago.

Stocks of both durable and non-durable goods piled up in August. There were large increases in unsold stocks of long-lasting goods like lumber, metals, hardware and new cars, as well bigger inventories of more-quickly used petroleum, groceries and chemicals.

The report was consistent with other signs of slowing second-half economic activity. Weaker sales generally lead to reduced output of many goods, which already is showing up in a slackening pace of business for many manufacturing industries.
During August, total wholesale sales dropped 0.9 percent to a seasonally adjusted $200.20 billion -- the biggest monthly fall-off since a 1 percent decline in January.
That followed a downwardly revised 1.8 percent gain in July sales that previously was reported as a 2.4 percent increase.
As a result, the inventory-to-sales ratio that measures how long it would take to deplete inventories at the current sales pace rose to 1.30 months' worth from 1.28 months in July.
